title: Draw Your Go-to-Market Resource Graph
summary: One command draws every connector, model, segment, play, tool and agent in your go-to-market and how they connect, as a Mermaid flowchart or JSON: from the live Cargo workspace, or offline from your repository with the next deploy's changes marked.
body_markdown:
**To draw your go-to-market resource graph, run` cargo-ai project graph` : it prints every resource in your Cargo workspace (connectors, models, segments, plays, tools, agents and the rest) and what each one points at, as a Mermaid flowchart.** Add` --project` to draw your repository instead, offline, and` --plan` to colour what the next deploy would create, update or delete.


Mermaid renders in GitHub, in most docs tools and in coding agents, so the graph can go straight into a README or a pull request comment.


## The commands#


shellscript


```text
npm   install   -g   @cargo-ai/cli
cargo-ai   login   --email   you@company.com


cargo-ai   project   graph                            # the live workspace, as Mermaid
cargo-ai   project   graph   --project                  # the local project, offline, no API calls
cargo-ai   project   graph   --project   --plan           # mark what the next deploy changes
cargo-ai   project   graph   --json   >   graph.json        # the same graph as JSON


```


` cargo-ai cdk graph` and the standalone` cargo-cdk graph` are the same command.` --plan` only works with` --project` , because the diff is between your code and its deploy state.


## What comes back#


A Mermaid flowchart, left to right. Each resource is a node labelled with its kind and name, folders become nested subgraphs, and the arrow says what the edge means:


text


```text
flowchart LR
subgraph n0["Outbound"]
n4["play: Expansion"]
end
n1["connector: HubSpot"]
n2["model: contacts"]
n3["segment: Expansion targets"]
n1 -.-> n2
n2 -.-> n3
n3 -.-> n4
n4 -->|"updateContact"| n1


```


That is the shape, not output from a real workspace. The edge kinds, read from source to target:


Edge Meaning


` uses` calls a connector: a workflow action, an agent’s model or MCP server


` feeds` records flow: a connector into its model, a model into a segment, play or agent


` calls` invokes a tool, agent, worker, MCP server or app


` triggers` a play starts the play scheduled after it; a connector’s events start an agent


` parent` a model unified under a parent model


` relates` a relationship between two models


` watches` an alert over a play, tool, agent or model


With` --plan` , created resources are green, updated ones amber and deleted ones red and dashed.


` --json` prints a versioned` CargoGraph` object (` version` ,` source` ,` workspace` ,` nodes` ,` edges` ,` unresolved` ,` integrations` ).` unresolved` lists references the graph does not contain, such as a resource deleted outside the project or a` modelRef` to something the project does not declare. A workspace graph also carries each integration’s logo and colour; a project graph read offline does not.


## When to use which#


- **The workspace graph** answers “what is actually running”: everything in the workspace, including resources nobody declared in code.
- **The project graph** answers “what does this repository declare”, and needs no login. If a resource file fails to load, the command prints the errors and exits rather than drawing a graph that silently omits the broken resources.
- **The plan graph** is a review aid: paste it into a pull request so a reviewer sees which part of the engine a change touches. On a[connected repository](https://www.getcargo.ai/blog/deploy-go-to-market-changes-on-merge) , the plan comment already lists the changes and[what the merge sends](https://www.getcargo.ai/blog/preview-go-to-market-changes-before-merge) .


To draw a single play, tool or run step by step rather than the whole workspace, use` cargo-ai orchestration node diagram` .


More on the lifecycle:[GTM as code: the complete guide](https://www.getcargo.ai/blog/gtm-as-code-complete-guide) . Every resource the graph can contain is declared with the[Cargo CDK](https://www.getcargo.ai/cdk) .
